raw_case_text:
A 58-year-old Hispanic female with a distant history of coccidioidomycosis diagnosed 20 years ago was admitted to Kern Medical Center through the emergency department (ED) with a one-month history of progressive right-sided chest pain and dyspnea. Her symptoms were accompanied by unintended weight loss of 15 pounds over the past month, intermittent subjective fevers, and chills for one week. Her family noted that she appeared increasingly frail, with a slow gait and significant weakness. Four months prior to admission, the patient attended the Kern County Fair, where she consumed nacho chips with cheese. This was followed by a one-month episode of diarrhea, after which her current symptoms gradually developed. She also reported a history of travel to Mexico one year ago. On admission, the patient presented with the following vital signs: blood pressure (BP) 100/60 mmHg, temperature 38.2 C, pulse 103/minute, and respiratory rate 28/minute. She was not in respiratory distress but had diminished breath sounds in the right lower lung and mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen.
Laboratory results (Table 1) revealed elevated alkaline phosphatase (215 U/L), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (95 mm/h), and C-reactive protein (10.4 mg/dL); hemoglobin (Hb: 9.8 g/dL); normal white blood cell (WBC) count: 7.7 x 103/mcL; normal transaminases and bilirubin levels; normal creatinine level. Serology tests for coccidioidomycosis, HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B and C were negative.
A CT chest scan showed an elevated right hemidiaphragm with a heterogeneous 12 cm mass in the right hepatic lobe. An abdominal ultrasound (Figure 1) revealed a solid mass in the right hepatic lobe near the dome of the liver measuring 12.9 x 9.8 x 9.6 cm, raising concerns for malignancy.
A subsequent CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast (Figure 2) confirmed a lobulated, hypodense, non-cystic lesion measuring 14 x 10 x 13 cm. 
Tumor markers (AFP, CA 19-9, and CEA) were normal. Hydatid cysts were initially considered but ruled out based on the absence of cystic features on imaging. The patient underwent an ultrasound-guided liver biopsy, yielding approximately 500 mL of grayish purulent fluid. A drainage catheter was placed. Immediately post-procedure, she experienced a transient episode of hypotension and syncope, which resolved with intravenous fluids. Cultures of the aspirate and blood were negative for bacterial growth. Magnetic resonance imaging (Figure 3) performed two days after drainage showed a reduction in lesion size from 14 x 10 x 13 cm to 10.8 x 7.2 x 9.6 cm.
Given her travel history and clinical presentation, serology for Entamoeba histolytica was performed and came back positive for E. histolytica IgG antibodies. Based on the serological results, clinical symptoms, and imaging findings, a diagnosis of amebic liver abscess (ALA) was made.
The patient was started on oral metronidazole 750 mg three times daily, which led to rapid improvement in fever, weakness, and anorexia. She was hospitalized for ten days and discharged with continued oral metronidazole.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old Hispanic female presented with a 1-month history of progressive right-sided chest pain, dyspnea, and 15-pound unintentional weight loss, along with 1 week of intermittent fevers and chills.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Four months prior to admission, the patient attended the Kern County Fair and consumed nacho chips with cheese, followed by a 1-month episode of diarrhea. Subsequently, over the month prior to admission to Kern Medical Center, she developed progressive right-sided chest pain, dyspnea, a 15-pound unintentional weight loss, frailty, slow gait, anorexia, and significant weakness, with intermittent subjective fevers and chills during the week before presentation.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of coccidioidomycosis diagnosed 20 years ago. Travel history to Mexico 1 year prior to admission; attended the Kern County Fair 4 months prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right-sided chest pain, dyspnea, 15-lb weight loss, frailty, weakness, slow gait, anorexia, intermittent fevers, chills, and prior 1-month diarrheal illness.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs on admission: blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, temperature 38.2 C, heart rate 103 beats/min, and respiratory rate 28 breaths/min. General: frail appearance, not in acute respiratory distress. Chest: diminished breath sounds in the right lower lung field. Abdomen: mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory results: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, normal WBC count 7.7 x 10^3/mcL, elevated alkaline phosphatase 215 U/L, normal transaminases and bilirubin, normal creatinine, elevated ESR 95 mm/h, and elevated CRP 10.4 mg/dL. Serologies for coccidioidomycosis, HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C were negative. Abdominal ultrasound revealed a 12.9 x 9.8 x 9.6 cm solid-appearing mass in the right hepatic lobe near the hepatic dome. Blood cultures were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: CT chest showed an elevated right hemidiaphragm and a heterogeneous 12 cm mass in the right hepatic lobe. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis confirmed a lobulated, hypodense, non-cystic right hepatic lesion measuring 14 x 10 x 13 cm. Serum tumor markers (AFP, CA 19-9, and CEA) were normal. Ultrasound-guided liver biopsy/aspiration yielded ~500 mL of grayish purulent fluid with drainage catheter placement (complicated by transient post-procedural hypotension and syncope responsive to IV fluids); aspirate bacterial cultures were negative. Follow-up abdominal MRI 2 days post-drainage showed reduction of the lesion to 10.8 x 7.2 x 9.6 cm.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Serological testing returned positive for Entamoeba histolytica IgG antibodies (with malignancy, hydatid disease, bacterial abscess, and recurrent coccidioidomycosis ruled out), confirming an amoebic liver abscess. Following ultrasound-guided aspiration (500 mL) and catheter drainage, the patient was treated with oral metronidazole 750 mg three times daily, resulting in rapid resolution of fever, weakness, and anorexia; she was discharged after a 10-day hospitalization to complete oral metronidazole.
